youtube_title: The White Hurricane of 1913: the storm that tore up Michigan City's lighthouse pier
youtube:
In November 1913, the worst storm in Great Lakes history blew for four days. 🌊 Sailors called it the White Hurricane: hurricane-force winds, whiteout snow, 35-foot waves. About a dozen ships sank and roughly 250 sailors died, most of them on Lake Huron. At the south end of Lake Michigan, Chicago's new Lincoln Park breakwater was wrecked, and in Michigan City, Indiana, the waves tore away about 200 feet of the elevated catwalk out to the East Pierhead lighthouse. To reach the light, the keepers rode a breeches buoy, a canvas seat on a rope slung over the gap. No ship was lost near Michigan City; the only one lost with her crew on Lake Michigan went down at the mouth of Green Bay. The 1904 lighthouse is still standing on the pier today.
